output.name: Ketrun

anatomy.part: top spar of the kite, its crown
left point of the kite, the wingtip where the bridle string is tied
lower point of the kite, where the tail hangs
the flier's hand at the knot, where the flying line leaves the kite
the bridle knot below the hand, where the plumb line is let down
a bead on the plumb line
a lower bead on the plumb line
the lead weight at the end of the plumb line

output.myth: When Aun cut the string he did not know how far the sky went, so he asked Ennu for a measure. Ennu the Kite-Wright sewed a kite of sailcloth and hung a lead on its tail, the way a fisherwife weights a net. They let out line bead by bead, the lead sinking as the kite rose. Hesk watched from the pole and counted every knot. She keeps count of whatever is let go. When the lead touched the place where the wind stands still, Aun shouted that he had found the bottom of the air. Tavo heard, laughed, and the gale tore the kite loose at the knot. The lead still hangs somewhere, and the line runs down to the islands. On a still day, if the string goes heavy in your hand, that is the lead, still falling.
output.verse:
Lead on the long line,
Hesk keeps count of every knot,
Drop it, read the wind.
